title: What We Know, and How We Know It: the King Street Trials
body: Captain Preston and eight soldiers were tried in Boston in the fall of 1770 — defended, at real cost to his practice, by John Adams. The testimony conflicts on almost everything that matters: whether Preston ordered 'Fire,' whether the word came from the crowd, whether bells meant fire-the-verb or fire-the-noun. Preston and six soldiers were acquitted; two were convicted of manslaughter, pleaded benefit of clergy, and were branded on the thumb. Adams called his defense 'one of the most gallant, generous, manly and disinterested actions of my whole life.' The scene you watched shows only what witnesses swore to — and where they disagreed, so does the camera.

quote.attribution: John Adams, closing argument, Rex v. Wemms (1770)
